verdict.rationale: Braintrust documents programmatic dataset creation through its API and SDKs. It also documents running evals from agent clients via its official MCP server and the `bt` CLI, and running experiments programmatically from code. Reading eval results back programmatically is only implied by "manage experiments" and log export, and no single documented agent flow ties all three steps together. missing for 10: explicit documentation of an agent reading back experiment/eval results via MCP or API, explicit MCP support for dataset creation, an end-to-end agent workflow example, independent hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent create a dataset, trigger an eval run programmatically, and read back the results

citations.quote: You can use it to: Create and manage projects, experiments, and datasets
Log traces, manage prompts, create datasets, and run evals or experiments right from your code.
Query production logs, author prompts and scorers, configure monitoring, and run evals from Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code, and any other MCP-compatible client.
It lets you authenticate, trace coding-agent sessions, run evals, browse and query logs, sync data, and manage functions without leaving your terminal.
lets you run experiments programmatically, and lets you integrate evals into your CI/CD pipeline
